The fluorescent hum of the Blackwood Bay archives was usually the loudest thing in the room, but a new, low thrum had settled into the foundations of everything lately. David Vance ignored it, mostly, tracing a finger over a faded microfilm image of a timber deed from 1987. The tremor, barely perceptible, made the worn wooden table beneath his elbow shiver, causing a stack of research folders to slide a fraction of an inch. It was less an earthquake, more a slow, geological sigh from deep beneath the peninsula, a sound that had become a constant companion in this town of secrets.

His portable scanner, usually reserved for police frequencies, sputtered to life with a crackle of static. He hadn't touched it. Amidst the white noise, a faint, almost melodic whisper rose, barely audible, then faded. "...Huang..." The name hung in the air, a ghost word, before dissolving back into the hiss and pop. David leaned closer to the microfilm, the image of the deed blurring slightly with the persistent hum. The details here, the shifting ownership of the old lighthouse property, felt disconnected, yet somehow resonant with the unspoken current running through Blackwood Bay. Everyone knew someone was always listening, always watching, but the how and why remained just out of reach, like that phantom whisper.
